slides.title: External Analysis: Macro-environment Impact of ICT
Value Mapping: Value Curve & Value Network

q1Macro.title: E-commerce & digital direct sales
q1Macro.what: ICT enables online ordering and transparent pricing, removing the dealership layer.
q1Macro.why: Significant because it changes customer-relationship ownership and sales-channel economics (Tesla, BYD online ordering).

q1Macro.title: Connected, software-defined vehicles with OTA
q1Macro.what: Cars become updatable platforms with over-the-air feature delivery.
q1Macro.why: Significant because revenue and value continue after sale, and quality & features improve without recalls.

q1Macro.title: Big data, AI & cloud
q1Macro.what: Fleet data feeds autonomy, battery optimization and predictive maintenance.
q1Macro.why: Significant because data becomes a competitive moat and a new service-revenue stream.

q1Structure.title: Digital charging & energy platforms, IoT & smart grid
q1Structure.what: Charging-network apps, plug-and-charge and V2G integrate utilities and mobility.
q1Structure.why: Significant because it creates new stakeholders and ecosystem power (Tesla Supercharger, BYD charging, Hyundai Ioniq charging partners).

q1Structure.title: Smart manufacturing & digital supply chain
q1Structure.what: Digital twins, robotics, IoT and AI (HMGICS) plus integrated battery supply (BYD Blade Battery).
q1Structure.why: Significant because it lowers entry barriers for tech-native players and shifts bargaining power toward integrated players.

fiveForces.note: Tech-native players enter via software & smart mfg
Vertical battery integration lowers supplier leverage

networkNodes.label: EV Customer
networkNodes.benefit: Lower cost, connected experience, continuous value

q3Changes.title: Direct-to-Consumer Online Ordering
q3Changes.to: Agency model: online orders, dealers become delivery & service agents
q3Changes.rationale: Shift in stakeholder relationship — OEM owns the customer, controls pricing and data.

q3Changes.title: Software-Defined Vehicle Subscriptions
q3Changes.to: OTA features, FSD / driver-assist and comfort packages as recurring revenue
q3Changes.rationale: Revenue-model shift from transactional to recurring, high-margin software income.

q3Changes.title: Battery-as-a-Service
q3Changes.to: Pay-per-use or swap, with second-life energy storage
q3Changes.rationale: Consumption shift lowers upfront cost and unlocks circular battery value.

q3Changes.title: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Energy Ecosystem
q3Changes.to: Car earns money for the owner by trading energy with utilities
q3Changes.rationale: New value network with utilities — vehicle becomes a distributed grid asset.

q3Changes.title: Mass-Customization via Smart Factories
q3Changes.rationale: Customer-preference shift to personalized, locally-produced vehicles.

items.text: Tesla leads e-business & software — direct sales, OTA, FSD and Supercharger network define the digital-native model.
BYD leads vertical integration & scale — Blade battery, in-house supply chain and volume dominance.
HMGICS leads manufacturing innovation (robotics, AI, digital twin) but is medium on customer-facing e-business as a production hub.
Mercedes EQS has a strong brand and medium readiness but a legacy-minded, dealer-bound model with slower OTA and direct-sales — at risk in software & direct channels.

takeaways: ICT turns cars into connected, software-defined platforms with recurring revenue.
Value shifts from one-time sales to services, data and energy ecosystems.
Vertical integration (BYD) and software leadership (Tesla) are the twin paths to lead.
Legacy OEMs must digitize sales & OTA fast or risk disruption.

speakerNotes.3: Open with the sales-channel disruption — Tesla proved direct online ordering works at scale. Emphasize that ICT doesn't just digitize the old process; it removes a whole layer (dealers) and shifts who owns the customer relationship. Tie each point back to e-business transformation.
speakerNotes.4: Frame these two as 'industry structure' not macro. Walk the radar: new entrants and rivalry spike up, supplier power drops thanks to vertical integration. Cite BYD Blade Battery and HMGICS smart factory as concrete evidence.
speakerNotes.5: Trace one company along the chain — BYD owns most of it, Tesla owns software & sales, HMGICS owns assembly. The overlays show who controls which stage; the more stages you own, the more digital value you capture.
speakerNotes.6: The value curve shows Tesla peaks on software & digital sales, Mercedes on luxury, BYD on price & sustainability. The network diagram is the screenshot moment — all flows converge on the EV customer, with benefit ranking showing OEMs and charging networks gain most.
speakerNotes.7: These five imagineered changes are the heart of Q3. For each, state the 'from → to' shift clearly and the stakeholder it affects. V2G and BaaS are the most radical — the car becomes a revenue source, not just a cost.
speakerNotes.8: Read the heat-map left to right per company. Tesla is all green, BYD mostly green with two ambers, HMGICS strong only on smart mfg, Mercedes amber across with a direct-sales weakness. Overall: Tesla & BYD High, HMGICS & Mercedes Medium.
speakerNotes.9: Deliver the verdict crisply: Tesla & BYD are the leaders for different reasons, HMGICS is a strong manufacturing challenger, Mercedes carries disruption risk in software and direct sales. Always cite the reason.
